customCommands.name: bug-version
customCommands.description: Copy the current project and inject real bugs for a bug-hunt drill
customCommands.prompt:
Run this command in the terminal, then read BUG_VERSION_MANIFEST.json and summarise every injected bug with its file, line, and impact:

python {ROOT}/.bug/scripts/make_bug_version.py . --profile messy --count 12

If the `bug` command is on PATH, you can also use:

bug bug-version . --profile messy --count 12

After it completes, open BUG_VERSION_MANIFEST.json and explain what broke and why each mutation would cause a test failure or runtime regression.

customCommands.name: bug-inject
customCommands.description: Inject bugs into a sandbox directory in-place (training/examples only)
customCommands.prompt:
Run this in the terminal:

python {ROOT}/.bug/scripts/inject_bug.py {input} --profile messy --count 3

Then read BUG_INJECTION_REPORT.json and describe every mutation: which file, which line, what changed, and how to reproduce the failure.

Replace {input} with the target sandbox path the user provided.

customCommands.name: bug-chaos
customCommands.description: Generate a maximum-difficulty bug version (chaos profile)
customCommands.prompt:
Run in the terminal:

python {ROOT}/.bug/scripts/make_bug_version.py . --profile chaos --count 20

Then read BUG_VERSION_MANIFEST.json and create a structured bug-hunt challenge with:
1. A list of changed files (no line numbers — keep it a puzzle)
2. Reproduction steps for each bug
3. A hidden answer key at the bottom under a <details> block
